notes.purpose: MySQL 8.4. It overrides nothing, and that is the finding rather than the starting point: this leaf was written empty on purpose, and the oracle was asked whether the claim held. It did. The corpus agrees entry for entry, the same expressions are refused, all 10 row rules agree, and 6,000 generated programs produce numbers identical to MariaDB's.
notes.how-it-was-authored: By writing `extends: mysql-family` and nothing else, regenerating, and running php/bin/sqlo against a real MySQL 8.4.11. That is the reverse of how mariadb.json was authored -- read the manual, write the templates, hope -- and it is the cheaper order once an oracle exists: the server enumerates the differences instead of a person trying to remember them. There were none.
notes.version: 8.4 is the minimum this document assumes and what every `since` is compared against. The regex functions the family relies on -- REGEXP_INSTR, REGEXP_REPLACE -- arrived in 8.0.4, so a 5.7 leaf would need most of the regex family refused; it is not written because nobody has probed one.
notes.sql_mode: Verified on 8.4.11 with the shipped default: ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY, STRICT_TRANS_TABLES, NO_ZERO_IN_DATE, NO_ZERO_DATE, ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO, NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION. The family's textEscape assumption is that NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES is off, which it is. ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO governs INSERT and UPDATE, not SELECT: SELECT 1/0 is still NULL here, exactly as on MariaDB, which is the divergence docs/SQL-TRANSLATION.md §11.1 records.
notes.identical-by-check: Two checks in php/bin/sqlt, and they guard different halves. The case mirror re-runs every mariadb case under mysql and requires the same string, the same error and the same parameters -- see MIRRORS there; it compares output, so a caveat is invisible to it, a caveat changing no output character. mirror_parity compares the two leaves entry by entry through Map::entries, which does include `caveat`, so a caveat added to one leaf and not the other fails too -- unless it is named in MIRROR_EXCEPTIONS with a reason, which skel.case is and is the only one. So this file staying empty is not an assumption anybody has to remember: adding any override to one leaf without the other fails the suite, and silencing that by widening MIRROR_EXCEPTIONS is itself mutation-tested (mirror-exception-is-not-guarded).
notes.where-they-do-differ: One place, found by extending the corpus past the range a rule normally reaches: DECIMAL caps the scale of a product, at 30 here and at 38 on MariaDB, so 0.00000000000000000000000000000001 * 2 is 2e-32 on MariaDB and zero here. That is declared by the scale-limit caveat on mysql-family's `*` rather than by an override on this leaf, because both servers truncate and only the digit they stop at differs -- the corpus carries one expression past each boundary so the caveat is seen doing work on both. So `identical to MariaDB's` above means identical below 30 fractional digits, and this file is still empty.
notes.where-mariadb-differs: mariadb.json is no longer empty either, and this leaf is why. MariaDB gives a CASE over NUM branches one type and pads the scale: CASE WHEN FALSE THEN 2.50 ELSE 3 END is 3.00 there and 3 here, which is what SEL says. So the override is on MariaDB, this file stays empty, and `identical-by-check` below means identical apart from the entries MariaDB declares an override for. LEN(IF(FALSE, 2.50, 3)) is the corpus line: 1 in SEL and here, 4 on MariaDB.
